intro: Healthy eating on a budget is a planning skill. Protein, fibre, and energy awareness do not require luxury groceries — they require a repeatable basket.
buddyTip: Buy protein in forms you’ll actually cook: eggs, dairy, frozen fish, legumes, chicken on offer — not Instagram ingredients.
mission: Build a three-day budget menu using foods already priced in your usual shop; log one of those meals today.
why: People abandon nutrition goals when food costs spike or cooking time explodes. Budget coaching keeps Scale Health Success realistic for families and students — not only for boutique meal-kit users.
Cost per protein gram and cost per satisfying meal matter more than organic labels. Eggs, oats, beans, frozen vegetables, potatoes, yoghurt/quark, and store-brand staples do serious work.
Waste is a hidden budget killer. Planning leftovers and freezing extras is health infrastructure.

what.lead: A budget-friendly pattern still hits the kCal priorities.
points: Prioritise protein staples on sale; freeze portions
Use legumes and dairy/eggs as affordable anchors
Frozen veg equals fresh for most fibre goals
Cook once, eat twice — intentional leftovers
Limit specialty “health” products that cost more than they help

misconceptions.myth: Healthy food is always more expensive.
misconceptions.truth: Ultra-processed convenience and frequent delivery often cost more than simple home staples.
Budget means choosing cheaper protein forms and cooking them well — not skipping protein.

how.lead: Shop with a protein-and-plants list, not aisle inspiration.
steps: Set a weekly food number before you enter the store or app
List protein anchors first, then fibre sides, then carbs/fats
Compare unit prices; favour family packs you can freeze
Log homemade meals — homemade does not mean “estimate zero oil”
Review monthly: which cheap meals did you happily repeat?
how.buddyHelps: Meal Plan and repeatable Foodiary entries make budget patterns visible. Buddy estimates still need your honest oils and portions.

sections.title: High-value basket examples
paras: Eggs + frozen veg + potatoes; oat porridge + quark; lentil soup + bread; tuna/bean salads; chicken batch-cook with rice and carrots.
Adapt to Finnish/German store realities: use what is on offer locally — the pattern matters more than the brand.

sections.title: Time is money
paras: If delivery saves a crisis night occasionally, log it and move on. If delivery is nightly, the budget and nutrition both erode — fix the plan and freezer first.

mistakes.quote: I bought expensive superfoods and still skipped protein.
mistakes.why: Misallocated budget. Fund anchors before accessories.

mistakes.quote: I only buy fresh salad leaves that wilt by Wednesday.
mistakes.why: Waste taxes your budget. Use sturdy veg and frozen backups.

mistakes.quote: Budget weeks don’t count for Progress.
mistakes.why: They are real life. Log them — Buddy should learn your actual pattern.

encouragement: Constraint can sharpen skills. A simple, protein-forward basket repeated weekly is elite behaviour in ordinary clothes.
